Things I have built

Things I built because the idea would not leave me alone.

Robots, vehicles, furniture, electronics, simulations, retro computing experiments and workshop archaeology.

The good ones

Start here.

Robot Arm

I wanted somewhere to run policies trained in MuJoCo and find out what the simulator had been quietly lying about. So: printed cycloidal joints, servo drives, a bus, and considerably more wiring than the CAD suggested. Still in progress.

Open project

MSc Artificial Intelligence

After twenty-odd years of building production systems I went back and did the maths properly. Nine taught modules, from sandwich ontologies to reinforcement learning, and a dissertation on robot learning.

Open project

Corten Balustrade

The terrace needed an edge and I could not face a bought-in railing. Curved weathering steel, checked with FEA before cutting anything expensive, then left outside to rust on purpose.

Open project

CV in a Box

I wanted to know whether a CV people pick up beats a CV people skim, so I packaged myself like a 1990s software product. Box art included.

Open project

Drift Trike

An electric trike built to go sideways, for a small and extremely demanding test driver. Steel frame, hub motor, and a lot of welding through a green filter.

Open project

Mega Book Case

A wall of books, built in sections around an existing window. Then it needed a rolling ladder, which became its own project with machining and welding in it.

Open project

Also written up

Steel, timber, light, electronics and one surfboard.

Spiral Staircase

The courtyard needed a way upstairs that did not eat the whole courtyard. Curved steel, fitted around a building that was already there and nowhere near square.

Curving Skirting Board

I built a house with curved walls, which meant the skirting board had to be steam-bent to follow them. Hence a timber sauna on the terrace.

Motorised Standing Desk

A height-adjustable desk built with my son, mostly as an excuse to spend a day in the workshop with him.

Lathe Sparks

Hardened steel, a CBN insert and an old Colchester Chipmaster. There is no lesson here, it just looks awesome.

3D Printer Build

An Original Prusa MK4 kit, built over Christmas. It now quietly manufactures the parts for everything else on this page.

Vintage String Lights

Shop-bought lighting would have lit the room. I wanted it to feel like somewhere specific, so: twisted cable, warm filament bulbs and made fittings.

BEng Chess Board

Final-year Mechatronics project from Leeds: a robotic chessboard, hand-wound electromagnets and report scans from 1997.

Belly Board

Won a competition, spent the prize on a day course shaping a wooden belly board in Cornwall.
